subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
subtype: Approach: adjusting when the plan meets reality [Revision]
passage:
Friday, 9:40 pm
Okay, my brain is still buzzing. The storm knocked half the neem tree onto Temple Road, right on our practised route to the school shelter. My stomach dropped, because in every drill the road was clear! Papa was ahead with Ajji, who was slow, and she was holding his sleeve. I remembered: don't force it, don't climb over branches. A volunteer in an orange vest, Hemant, waved us toward the lane behind the dairy and called me beti and said it was longer but open. Ajji hated the extra walk but held my arm. On the way I texted the family group: "Temple Rd blocked. Taking dairy lane. Meet at the school BACK gate now, not the front." Mummy replied with 👍. We got there at 8:15. Note to self: every plan needs a Plan B, and the group gets told the second it changes.
- Ganga

qa.q: Which lane did the volunteer point them to?
qa.a: The volunteer waved them toward the lane behind the dairy.

qa.q: What was Ganga feeling when she saw the tree on the route?
qa.a: She was shocked and afraid: her stomach dropped because in every drill the road was clear. 😰

qa.q: What could Ganga do if the dairy lane were also blocked, and why?
qa.a: She could ask the volunteers for another safe way, or wait with an adult at a safe spot and update the family group, because forcing a way through debris is risky.

qa.q: How might Ajji see the changed plan?
qa.a: Ajji disliked the extra walk but held Ganga's arm, so Ajji may have felt tired yet glad to be led safely.

grounding: When debris blocks the planned route, a teen takes an alternate way from volunteers, then updates the family group and the meeting point.

Family group
Reena: at the school gate. main road to the relief camp is blocked, a tree and a wall came down
Thomas: are you safe?
Reena: yes. volunteers here are sending people by the canal road instead, they're walking with groups
Thomas: that's longer. are you sure?
Reena: they know the area, they've checked it. i'm going with their group of 12
Reena: new plan: canal road, then the back gate of the camp, not the front
Thomas: ok. i'll meet you at the back gate then
(35 min later)
Reena: reached back gate. with the group. wet but ok
Thomas: i see you. waving
Reena: telling Mum in her chat too, she's coming from the hospital side

qa.q: What blocked the main road to the relief camp?
qa.a: A tree and a wall came down.

qa.q: How does Reena seem to feel when the main road is blocked?
qa.a: Reena seems calm and practical, trusting the volunteers and quickly making a new plan rather than panicking.

qa.q: What else could Reena do before setting off with the group?
qa.a: Share the volunteers' route and a rough arrival time with the family, so they know when to start worrying.

qa.q: What is the change like for Thomas?
qa.a: Thomas is anxious at first about the longer route, but the clear update lets him wait at the right gate.

grounding: Shows a teen calmly taking an alternate route suggested by volunteers when the planned road is blocked, and updating the family group and meeting point.

passage:
The plan was simple: if the river rose, Bhavna would take her little brother Sumit up the temple path to the school on the hill, where the family would meet. But when they reached the bend, a landslip had buried the path under mud and rocks.
Sumit started to cry. Bhavna's heart was pounding, but she crouched and held his shoulders. “We'll find another way.”
Two panchayat volunteers in orange vests stood at the bend, turning people back. “Go round by the fields and the water tank,” one said. “It's longer but it's safe; we checked it an hour ago.”
Bhavna nodded and took the fields path, holding Sumit's hand. On the way she messaged the family group from Ma's old phone: “Temple path blocked. Going by the water tank. Meet at the school's side gate, not the front.”
Forty minutes later, Ma and Baba were waiting at the side gate.

qa.q: What had buried the temple path?
qa.a: A landslip had buried the path under mud and rocks.

qa.q: What was Bhavna feeling when she saw the blocked path?
qa.a: Bhavna was frightened, heart pounding, but calmed herself to comfort Sumit.

qa.q: Why was trusting the volunteers' route a good choice?
qa.a: They had checked it an hour ago and knew the area, so it was safer than guessing or climbing over the landslip.

qa.q: How was the walk for Sumit?
qa.a: Sumit was scared and crying at first, but a steady hand and the new route got him safely to Ma and Baba.

grounding: Shows a teen calmly taking a safer route suggested by volunteers when the planned path is blocked, and updating the family group and meeting point.
